title: Benchmarking the fermionic quasi-1D many-body problem
abstract: We investigate the validity of effective one-dimensional models for quasi-1D fermionic systems by benchmarking a coupled-channel approach against the exact low-energy theory derived from the underlying three-dimensional problem in the weakly and strongly attractive limits. We show that reproducing the exact two-body scattering amplitude is insufficient to construct the correct effective low-energy theory of quasi-1D fermions. In the weakly attractive regime, it does not capture the emergent three-body interaction induced by transverse excitations. In the strongly attractive regime, it yields an atom-dimer scattering length with an incorrect dependence on the three-dimensional scattering length. These results demonstrate the limitations of effective one-dimensional descriptions based solely on two-body physics and highlight the need to explicitly include few-body correlations in quasi-1D systems.
summary: The paper rigorously tests effective 1D models for fermionic quantum gases by comparing them against exact 3D theory. It demonstrates that while two-body physics can be captured, accurately describing three-body correlations—which arise from transverse excitations—requires explicitly incorporating higher-order terms into the Hamiltonian. This highlights a structural limitation in simple low-dimensional effective theories.
main_problem: The study investigates the limitations of using effective one-dimensional (quasi-1D) models to describe fermionic many-body physics in ultracold atomic gases.
main_result: Effective 1D descriptions based only on two-body interactions are insufficient; correctly modeling the system requires explicitly including emergent three-body correlations, especially near confinement-induced resonances.
method: The authors benchmarked a coupled-channel approach against exact low-energy theory derived from the underlying three-dimensional problem in both weakly and strongly attractive regimes.
model_or_system: The system involves quasi-1D fermionic gases confined in waveguides. The theoretical framework utilizes a coupled-channel Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{cc}$) to model interactions, comparing its predictions against exact T-matrix calculations.
key_observables: Two-body scattering amplitude ($f_k$), atom-dimer scattering length ($a_{AD}^{1D}$), and the emergent three-body interaction strength ($\hat{W}$).
important_parameters: Weakly attractive limit ($a_{3D} 	o 0^-$) and strongly attractive limit ($a_{3D} 	o 0^+$); transverse confinement size ($a_\perp$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on controlled approximations within the weakly and strongly attractive limits, though the structural failure suggests a need for fully non-perturbative treatment near resonances.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate effective parameters ($E_0$, $g_{1D}$, $\Gamma$) across different coupling regimes and show diagrammatic calculations of three-body scattering corrections ($\delta T_{AD}$ and $\delta T_{3b}$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the coupled-channel model to exact theory, first confirming success in reproducing two-body physics. It then demonstrates failures in capturing emergent three-body interactions in both weak and strong attraction limits, necessitating explicit higher-order terms.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it establishes fundamental theoretical boundaries for modeling strongly interacting quantum gases confined to low dimensions, guiding the development of more accurate many-body Hamiltonians.
